title: Melrose YMCA Full Body 3x A Week
author: linuslift
desc: Embark on a transformative 12-week journey with the Melrose YMCA Full Body program, designed for beginners and focused on bodybuilding. This program features 36 sessions, each lasting about 60 minutes, combining essential exercises like the Chest Press, Lat Pulldown, and Seated Hamstring Curl to build strength and muscle across all major muscle groups. With a full gym setup, you'll engage in a variety of machine-based workouts that promote proper form and technique. Get ready to elevate your fitness game and achieve your goals with this structured and supportive training plan!

ex.note: Do not arch back when pressing and keep your feet position in front of you do not use them for leg drive. The goal is to only use your chest, make sure the seat is positioned so it’s comfortable.
You do not need crazy range of motion, set chest pad so you can comfortably grip the handles and pull back while also trying to retract your shoulder blades (this is called shrugging).
You also do not need crazy range of motion just think about pulling your elbows into your body and stopping once they hit your sides, go up but do not get a crazy deep stretch (above 120°)
Use whatever attachment you like. Elbows should be locked to sides and not moving during the movements. Full focus on pushing hands down without moving elbows.
You can do dumbbell or barbell. Go all the way down and use a bench if possible at a high incline (higher than you think). Or use barbell. You will not tear a bicep going all the way down.
Whatever grip is comfortable, get good amount of range of motion.
Pull yourself hard into the seat and make sure you get full range of motion. Do the maximum weight you can possibly do and try your best to go as hard as possible.
Lock yourself tight into seat and get comfortable with the pads, adjust accordingly. Full range of motion here.
Go as far as you comfortably can.

Pull yourself hard into the seat and make sure you get full range of motion. Do the maximum weight you can possibly do and try your best to go as hard as possible.
Lock yourself tight into seat and get comfortable with the pads, adjust accordingly. Full range of motion here.
Go as far as you comfortably can.
Do not arch back when pressing and keep your feet position in front of you do not use them for leg drive. The goal is to only use your chest, make sure the seat is positioned so it’s comfortable.
You do not need crazy range of motion, set chest pad so you can comfortably grip the handles and pull back while also trying to retract your shoulder blades (this is called shrugging).
You also do not need crazy range of motion just think about pulling your elbows into your body and stopping once they hit your sides, go up but do not get a crazy deep stretch (above 120°)
Use whatever attachment you like. Elbows should be locked to sides and not moving during the movements. Full focus on pushing hands down without moving elbows.
